paragraphs.text: The meeting invite said fifteen minutes. It took six. Derek, the new vice president of operations, slid a printed spreadsheet across the table with my salary highlighted in yellow, like a coupon he'd found in the mail. Next to it, someone had typed one word in the notes column. Non-essential.

I'd held the state compliance license for eleven years. It's the reason our trucks are allowed to carry what they carry. Derek didn't ask what it did. He asked when I could have my desk cleared, and whether I'd mind leaving my badge with Janet at the front.

I said I'd have it done by four. Then I went back to my desk, opened a blank document, and started writing down every single thing my license signed off on, with the dates they were due. It came to nine pages. I printed two copies.
paragraphs.scene: typing on laptop keyboard at night
